candidate.authoritative_question: What minimal representation, currentness, and content bindings would let a multi-step epistemic intervention program be constructed as a non-executable candidate object from learned opaque structure, and what control would distinguish genuine construction from caller-supplied sequence encoding?
candidate.measurement_frame: Developmental pressure utilizing learned opaque structure and already-qualified primitive capabilities
candidate.probe: Can Microseed construct and arbitrate a useful multi-step epistemic intervention/program from organism-owned opaque action/outcome history and currently qualified primitive capabilities without the caller naming the preferred action or program sequence?
candidate.derive: Microseed can construct and arbitrate useful multi-step epistemic interventions/programs by leveraging learned opaque structure and already-qualified primitives, decoupling candidate construction from execution permission.
candidate.verify: The construction of useful multi-step epistemic interventions/programs from learned opaque structure and primitives is verified through the demonstration of candidate construction and arbitration mechanisms.
candidate.oarr: A rival mechanism could involve developing a new algorithm that incorporates both learned opaque structure and primitive capabilities to construct and arbitrate interventions/programs without caller-supplied action names.
candidate.loop_plus: Widening the causal explanation to include the role of developmental pressure in shaping the construction and arbitration of interventions/programs.
candidate.incumbent_hypothesis: Microseed can construct and arbitrate useful multi-step epistemic interventions/programs from learned opaque structure and primitives without the caller naming the preferred action or program sequence.
candidate.rival_hypothesis: A new algorithm that incorporates both learned opaque structure and primitive capabilities can construct and arbitrate interventions/programs without caller-supplied action names.
candidate.incumbent_prediction: Microseed will successfully construct and arbitrate a multi-step epistemic intervention/program from learned opaque structure and primitives without the caller naming the preferred action or program sequence.
candidate.rival_prediction: The new algorithm will successfully construct and arbitrate a multi-step epistemic intervention/program from learned opaque structure and primitives without the caller naming the preferred action or program sequence.
candidate.measurement: The success rate of constructing and arbitrating useful multi-step epistemic interventions/programs from learned opaque structure and primitives without the caller naming the preferred action or program sequence.
candidate.falsifier: A lower success rate in constructing and arbitrating useful multi-step epistemic interventions/programs from learned opaque structure and primitives without the caller naming the preferred action or program sequence.
candidate.minimal_embodiment: A new algorithm that incorporates both learned opaque structure and primitive capabilities to construct and arbitrate interventions/programs without caller-supplied action names.
candidate.stop_condition: The success rate of constructing and arbitrating useful multi-step epistemic interventions/programs from learned opaque structure and primitives without the caller naming the preferred action or program sequence is significantly higher for the incumbent hypothesis.
candidate.next_if_incumbent: How can Microseed ensure that the constructed interventions/programs are decoupled from execution permission while still being useful and effective?
